paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: The effect of context masking on case tasks groupby by language family. Error bars indicate the standard deviation.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks, grouped by language family, with error bars indicating the standard deviation for each model and language group. The horizontal axis displays eight language family categories: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic family, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis, labeled “effect,” is measured on a linear scale ranging from 0 to 30, with tick marks at intervals of 10. For each language family, six colored bars represent the performance of different multilingual BERT models: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light pink), and XLM-B₂ (dark red). The bars are grouped side-by-side within each language family, with their heights indicating the magnitude of the effect. For example, in the IE-Indic family, the tallest bar is mBERT-R₂ (light green) with an effect of approximately 20, followed closely by mBERT-B₂ (light pink) at about 22, while the shortest bars are mBERT-L₂ (light blue) and XLM-L₂ (dark blue), both at approximately 1. In the Semitic family, the tallest bar is XLM-B₂ (dark red) at approximately 20, followed by XLM-L₂ (dark blue) at about 15, and mBERT-L₂ (light blue) at approximately 10. The chart does not show any explicit sorting of bars within each group, and no bars are visually emphasized with shading, bolding, or annotations beyond the standard error bars.
